To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the most common reasons for citing literature are to (1) provide evidence of a point of view; (2) to show that one’s work is novel; (3) to provide a concept marker; (4) to provide a well-known work; (5) to provide a review; and (6) to provide an opportunity for criticism.

authors in the field of communication are more likely than those in psychology to cite works for reasons related to the authority of their own work and less likely for reasons related to their personal connection to the cited work or to its content.
authors are motivated to cite works because they are novel and/or well-known, and because they are likely to be concept markers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: “What do authors think about when they decide to cite a document?”
the reasons why authors cite literature, and the ways in which citation is a rhetorical strategy.
the question of what motivates authors to cite other works, and the answers to this question are of interest to both researchers and practitioners in the field of communication.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
authors cite works for a variety of reasons.
authors in communication tend to cite literature for a mix of reasons that are both similar to and different from those of other disciplines.
authors in communication are motivated to cite works that have a high degree of creativity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reasons for citing literature vary according to the nature of the cited work, the relationship between citers and cited authors, and the citers’ motivations.
the most common reason for citing literature is to support the authority of one's own work.
authors cite literature to establish the authority of their work, to demonstrate that their work is novel and well-known, and to criticize the works of others.
The main takeaway from our work is that
authors’ motivations for citing literature are complex and multidimensional.
citation is a complex phenomenon that requires more sophisticated research methods than those typically employed.
citation is a complex phenomenon, and that it is difficult to predict why a given work will be cited.
